title: The Stair Step Method: how bootstrappers go from first product to recurring revenue
summary: Rob Walling lays out a repeatable three-step path he saw among bootstrappers who quit their jobs. Start with a simple add-on product on one free traffic channel. Repeat it until you own your time. Then build a recurring-revenue SaaS, where higher LTV unlocks paid channels.

principles.text: Make your first product simple, with a simple marketing plan that needs only one traffic channel.
principles.quote: The strategy that seems to give people the best chance of success is creating a simple product, with a simple marketing plan — one that only requires a single traffic channel.

principles.text: Don't start with a stand-alone SaaS. Sell an add-on to an existing ecosystem that gives you built-in discovery.
principles.quote: It’s much easier to sell an add-on to an existing ecosystem like a WordPress plugin, a Shopify app, a Heroku add-on — they’re usually small things to build, relatively inexpensive for customers to purchase, and you have built-in discovery through the plugin repository or app store.

principles.text: Master one traffic source first instead of learning every channel at once.
principles.quote: As for a single traffic source, focus on figuring out one way of generating customers, instead of trying to master all the different traffic channels at once.

principles.text: Double down on what worked until you own your time. Don't abandon it for a bigger challenge too early.
principles.quote: One of the biggest mistakes I see founders make is abandoning what already works and trying to take on a bigger challenge before they’re making enough money to own all of their time in a given week.

principles.text: Low-LTV products can't support paid ads or content marketing. Stick to free organic channels until LTV rises.
principles.quote: But when you’re selling something that has an LTV of $10-15 dollars, you just can’t make paid advertising work.

principles.text: Recurring revenue lifts LTV and opens up paid marketing, but has a long ramp, so do it after steps 1 and 2.
principles.quote: But the other side of the SaaS coin is that there’s a long ramp to any kind of substantial revenue, which is why I recommend you complete steps 1 and 2 before moving to this step.
